claims.text: Deliberate compositional tuning of key 3d magnetic elements can tune magnetic ordering in non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
Deliberate compositional tuning of key 3d magnetic elements can tune the magnetocaloric effect in non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
Composition affects magnetic behavior by modulating magnetic exchange interactions and spin fluctuations.
The baseline material is a non-equiatomic HEA containing several 3d transition metals.
Systematically varying the elemental ratios of magnetic elements is the proposed tuning intervention.
Composition and synthesis conditions can determine whether an HEA remains a single-phase solid solution or becomes multiphase.
Compositional changes produce local lattice distortions and changes in chemical short-range order.
Local lattice distortions and chemical short-range order mediate exchange interactions between spins.
Changing the relative concentrations of 3d magnetic elements changes the strength and balance of ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic interactions.
Changes in ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic interactions alter critical magnetic temperatures.
Changes in ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic interactions alter the magnetic entropy change.
Spin fluctuations modify the local magnetic or electronic state of 3d-transition-metal HEAs.
Compositional tuning will systematically shift the Curie temperature.
Compositional tuning will change the magnitude of the magnetocaloric effect.
An optimal composition can enhance magnetic entropy change sufficiently for low-dimensional magnetocaloric applications.
The useful compositional tuning range is limited by phase stability and solubility.
Changing composition beyond suitable limits may cause phase decomposition or secondary-phase formation.
The quantitative magnetocaloric response is uncertain because of interactions among composition, local structure, and magnetic behavior.
Curie temperature, magnetization curves, phase constitution, microstructure, and magnetic entropy change can be compared across a composition series.
A lack of statistically meaningful composition-dependent changes or correlations in Curie temperature and magnetocaloric performance would falsify the proposed tuning effect.
